Under the national Food Hygiene Rating Scheme, ratings range from 0, where urgent improvement is necessary, to 5, meaning hygiene standards are very good. The rating reflects the standards found on the date of the inspection and does not reflect the quality of the food. Businesses have the right to appeal a rating, to publish a reply alongside it, and to request a re-inspection once improvements have been made, so a rating listed here may since have changed. Each business's current rating is on the Food Standards Agency website.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale firm launching aerospace technology for the future - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An innovative Rochdale company is a real high flier in aerospace and defence. From precision engineering to next-generation aerospace technology, NEMA is helping put Rochdale on the global advanced manufacturing map. It was established in in 1954 as The Nordale Spring Company to supply the aerospace industry with components. In 2003, it changed its name to Nordale Electro-Mechanical Actuation (NEMA). For almost 70 years, NEMA has been designing and manufacturing precision-engineered motors, generators and components from its Rochdale base and has been supported on its journey by Rochdale Development Agency. Today, based at Chichester Business Centre, the company is recognised as one of the UK’s leading specialists in high-performance aerospace components, machinery and systems, supplying customers across the global aerospace and defence sectors. From concept development and prototyping through to qualification, production and aftermarket support, NEMA provides customers with complete engineering solutions that help bring advanced aerospace technologies into service with confidence. Then Mayor of Rochdale Cllr Janet Emsley speaks to NEMA staff. Image: Rochdale Council The business has developed expertise in electrification technologies that support the aviation sector’s transition towards more-electric and hybrid-electric aircraft, helping customers improve efficiency, reduce weight, increase reliability and lower environmental impact.

candidates.source_title: Double treat for town’s fish and chip lovers - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The fish and chip trade was booming in Middleton yesterday as Mother Hubbard opened its doors — and nearby Middleton Fish Bar sold out early. The Mother Hubbard franchise opened its Middleton Shopping Centre branch with a 45p fish-and-chip offer for the first 1,000 customers, which had people queueing back to the bus station. Among the first to sample the Mother Hubbard menu was Colin Thompson, who shared on My Rochdale’s Facebook page: “Fish n chips was awesome today, amazing staff and owners worked so hard today, they get my vote for chippy Friday every week.” Misa Ila agreed: “Great venue, good luck to them. The Rochdale one is mint.” Pat Keogh added: “Mother Hubbard’s, well done and good luck. Glad Middleton getting sorted now, it’s about time. Hope you do well.” As the steady stream of customers lined up outside the new chippy, traditional independent Middleton Fish Bar also reported booming trade, selling out and closing early at 2.30pm. Owners Paul and Caroline High shared: “Thank you to everyone who came through our doors, everyone who shared our posts, tagged us, commented, messaged and supported our family. Middleton Fish Bar enjoyed a roaring trade. Image: Middleton Fish Bar

candidates.source_title: Festival of Remembrance to be held at Rochdale Town Hall
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The event is being organised by Rochdale Borough Council with the local veterans’ community.

The evening will recognise the service and sacrifice of past and present Armed Forces personnel.

It will include music from military bands, an act of remembrance and historic war stories.

Guests are expected to include the Mayor of Rochdale, MPs, councillors and representatives from the Armed Forces.

Any money raised will go to the Mayor of Rochdale’s charities for 2026 and 2027.

They are Rochdale Veterans Breakfast Club, Rochdale Women’s Welfare Association, SANDS, Springhill Hospice and The Christie.

Mayor of Rochdale Councillor Faisal Rana said: “This will be a special evening as the Armed Forces community unites to pay its respect to the brave women and men for their service and sacrifice. It is sure to be a moving and memorable night in the stunning setting of the Great Hall at Rochdale Town Hall.

“We last held a Festival of Remembrance in 2019, so this will be a poignant occasion as we bring together the Armed Forces family under one roof. As a veteran, I understand the importance of recognising the service and sacrifice of our Armed Forces, as well as the council’s ongoing support for our military personnel.”

Tickets cost £15 and include a pie and pea supper.

They can be purchased through the Your Trust Rochdale website.
candidates.source_summary: A Festival of Remembrance will be held at Rochdale Town Hall on Friday 16 October to honour members of the Armed Forces community.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The cafe's manager, Lucy Traynor is the wife of Wayne, who is also a former veteran and co-director of Getting Together After Service (GTAS) A woman has said she was inspired to run a cafÃ© for veterans after witnessing the impact serving in the armed forces had had on her husband. Lucy Traynor's wife Wayne was temporarily blinded from an injury he suffered while serving. She became involved with charity Get Together After Serving (GTAS), which has renovated a 19th century manor house in Rochdale and now runs it as a cafÃ© staffed by former service personnel. Lucy said Denehurst House offered ex-servicepeople "somewhere to talk, somewhere they feel safe, somewhere people will listen and understand". Lucy added: "It's been these last 12 months that have been the biggest test for him, because he was diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder. "He's having really bad nightmares, which are completely affecting everyday life. So it's really hard watching." Denehurst House had been left empty for decades

candidates.source_title: Man arrested after tents found at Old Middleton Cemetery
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Middleton Labour said three people had been staying in tents at the cemetery, including two people described by the group as white British.

In an update published on social media, the councillors said police attended the site following a multi-agency meeting.

They said one man was arrested for immigration offences and detained by police before being referred to Immigration Enforcement.

The group said the other two people had been offered temporary accommodation but declined it.

Rochdale Council's rough sleepers outreach team had been working with the people for several weeks and would continue to offer support, according to the post.

Middleton Labour said all three people had now moved from the cemetery.

The council's Environmental Management Team was also sent to the site to remove rubbish, litter, fly-tipping, damaged bins and abandoned tents. Strimming work had also started.

The councillors said all three tents had been slashed overnight after posts circulated on social media describing the site as a "migrant camp".

They said police were looking for the person responsible and appealed for anyone with information to contact Greater Manchester Police on 101.

Middleton Labour also said police were monitoring social media after comments threatening violence were posted online.

People who experience hate crime or racial abuse were urged to report it to police.

Crimes can be reported to Greater Manchester Police on 101 or online, with 999 used in an emergency.

Rochdale Council's Community Safety Team can be contacted on 0300 303 8878 and its homelessness team on 0300 303 8875.
candidates.source_summary: The councillors also said the tents were slashed overnight and police are investigating.

candidates.source_title: 71-year-old man with dementia found near Piethorne Reservoir after search
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
A 71-year-old man with dementia was found cold and confused after a search involving police, mountain rescue volunteers and search dogs near Piethorne Reservoir in Newhey.

Oldham Mountain Rescue Team said it was called to assist Greater Manchester Police on 29 August after the man was reported missing.

Police believed the man could be in the Piethorne Reservoir area after an AirTag indicated he was nearby.

Initial police searches, including assistance from the National Police Air Service helicopter, had not located him.

Oldham Mountain Rescue Team was mobilised to the dam wall along with its water section.

Water rescue volunteers searched the water's edge on both sides of the dam, on foot and using a raft. Two other sections searched paths and tracks which police had not already covered.

Two Mountain Rescue Search Dogs England search dogs and their handlers were also called to assist.

The first search dog team was travelling to its allocated search area with a navigator from Oldham Mountain Rescue Team when they found the missing man.

The team said he was cold and confused when he was located.

He was walked a short distance to the mountain rescue control vehicle, where he was assessed before being handed over to police and his family for further checks.

Fifteen Oldham Mountain Rescue Team volunteers were involved in the callout, which lasted four and a half hours.
candidates.source_summary: A 71-year-old man with dementia was found cold and confused after a search involving police, mountain rescue volunteers and search dogs near Piethorne Reservoir in Newhey.

candidates.source_title: Council poised to purchase major Middleton landmark – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has struck a deal to acquire Middleton’s Warwick Mill, in a huge boost to the ongoing regeneration of the area. Built in 1907, the Grade II listed structure stopped operating as a cotton mill in 1965 and has been vacant for at least a decade. In recent years, alongside its neighbour, 1960’s office building, London House, which the council is also hoping to acquire under the terms of the deal, the site has become an eyesore and a target for vandalism. For the past decade the council has been working with the private sector to find a solution for the imposing structure but none of the plans came to fruition and its condition has been gradually deteriorating. The council has been looking at buying the mill for a period of time, but a recent engagement exercise with local residents and businesses galvanised their decision. The exercise, titled ‘Our Town, Our Future’ saw local community organisation, Middleton Co-operating, engage with more than 2,000 residents to find out what they wanted for the area as part of wider work to create a Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) for the area, which will be chaired by Middleton-born actor and comedian, Steve Coogan, and Rose Marley, chief executive of Co-operatives UK. Around a third of respondents said they would like to see Warwick Mill brought back into use. A number of people responding to the survey said that the building has huge potential and should be sensitively restored and brought back into use for the benefit of the wider community. candidates.source_title: Sports hub plan must tackle concerns over playing fields - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans for a football and community sports hub on playing fields in Middleton need to show the benefits outweigh any loss of current use, according to the body responsible for developing grass-roots sport. Sport England, which is a statutory consultee on key planning applications, has objected to Rochdale Council and Rochdale AFC’s plans for the hub at Bowlee Playing Fields. The plans are to create a training pitch for Rochdale AFC with a 3G pitch and grass pitch for Rochdale AFC Community Trust on one part of the council-owned site, with two 3G pitches and three grass pitches alongside cricket provision, a children’s playground and free parking for community use. As the plans affect the use of current playing fields, they have to meet one of Sport England’s five exception criteria in order for the body to support them. As well as changes to the existing playing field space and the exclusive use of certain areas by the club, Sport England raised concerns about the proposed Rochdale AFC pavilion’s community changing rooms. Its written response to the planning application states: “It is understood that the proposal would prejudice the use, or lead to the loss of use, of land being used as a playing field or has been used as a playing field in the last five years. An aerial view of the proposed Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields in Middleton shows Rochdale AFC’s hub in the foreground and the community pitches in the background. Image: Rochdale AFC Community Trust “The proposal is on playing fields which currently support the delivery of both football and cricket at the site and there are a number of outstanding issues which need to be resolved in order it to comply with Exception 5 criteria.
candidates.source_summary: Plans for a football and community sports hub on playing fields in Middleton need to show the benefits outweigh any loss of current use, according to the body responsible for developing grass-roots sport.
